_comment: Curated modulator side of the metabolic-modulation readout: one rule per (perpetrator, enzyme), joined at read time against the `metabolism` table's substrate side. The database already knows which enzyme clears which substance; it does not know which substances inhibit or induce an enzyme, and that is the only thing stated here. One row therefore fans out to every substance that enzyme clears — 152 for CYP3A4 — which is why this is not a pair table like drug_interactions_pk.
_strength: Qualitative only — weak | moderate | strong. A fold-change is never stored: the readout says which way exposure moves and roughly how hard, and no figure ships that would read as measured.

_origin.substance: A logged co-active drug. Fires in the interaction checker when both it and a substrate are selected.
_origin.context: A lifestyle flag that is never logged as a dose (grapefruit, tobacco smoke), so it carries no matchers and surfaces only as substance-page education.
_origin.self: A drug modulating the enzyme that clears itself, so repeated doses build up disproportionately.

_matchers: Lowercased names that identify the perpetrator in a logged dose. Their own relation, kept out of `aliases`: three of these perpetrators (grapefruit, ritonavir, rifampicin, St John's Wort) have no substances row at all, and armodafinil's names are alias rows on Modafinil — keying on substance_id would merge two rules that carry different copy. See the pharmacology_matchers schema comment.
_uncited: These are qualitative textbook classifications carried over from the app's original hardcoded catalog; no row carries a per-value citation yet. Worth grounding in the FDA Drug Development and Drug Interactions substrate/inhibitor/inducer table before any of them is restated as measured.

modulators.notes: The database's own drug_interactions_pk row for MDMA x ritonavir names CYP2D6 inhibition alongside CYP3A4. Only the 3A4 arm is curated here; a 2D6 rule would need its own sourced strength.
